description:
Scope and ownership: planning only; add tests exclusively in test/zaq/engine/channel_history_projection_test.exs for lib/zaq/engine/channel_history_projection.ex lines 283, 301, 318, 323, 341. Do not alter production code, existing admin/rating/LiveView tests, docs, or support code. No E2E (Engine read projection, no new user journey). Test-first, one issue/one Engine DB test surface. Existing coverage in test/zaq/engine/channel_history_admin_test.exs (thread/root/participants) and test/zaq/engine/scoped_channel_rating_test.exs (detail ratings) should be preserved, not duplicated.

Tests to add before implementation; use Zaq.DataCase, async: true unless inspecting existing fixture use demonstrates actual shared VM state; SQL Sandbox isolation per case. Exercise real ChannelHistoryProjection.project/1 with bounded, already-scoped row maps matching ChannelHistoryAdmin.dispatch(%{op: :list}) selection (id, parent_id, thread_id, owner_person_id, provider, channel_config_id, channel_name, etc.), persisted ChannelConfig/Transcript/Message/TranscriptMessage via public capture when suitable, and minimum explicit changeset-backed DB arrangement for deliberately incomplete historic rows. A thin super-admin :list route assertion may replace direct projection where security context matters; never treat direct project/1 as authorization proof. Existing People.create_person/1, People.add_channel/1, HistoryIngress.capture/1 and Conversations.capture_canonical_message/3 patterns from channel_history_admin_test.exs and Transcript.changeset/2, TranscriptMessage.changeset/2 from canonical_storage_test.exs are the reusable fixture examples. Keep important overrides inline; do not create shared support fixtures speculatively.

1) Line 283: persisted transcript with only an assistant placement (no eligible first non-assistant message); project its real scoped parent row; assert channel_name equals supplied connector/room fallback exactly and root_message nil. Also assert baseline non-assistant message with supported title_style still derives Person title, so fallback is discriminating. Avoid an empty unpersisted row as the sole proof.
2) Line 301: first non-assistant message has history_context title_style person_subject, author_person_id absent from loaded People (prefer a non-existent integer; no Person insertion), author_name "Archived sender", subject "Follow-up"; assert projected channel_name "Archived sender: Follow-up" (and not fallback title). Arrange canonical message through capture, then use Message changeset update if capture sanitizes context; do not fake people map or private calls. Include author_name nil with author_id "external-peer" only if the first case does not sufficiently distinguish fallback precedence; assert "external-peer: Follow-up". Missing subject can separately assert "(No subject)" if not already covered elsewhere.
3) Line 318: persisted thread root message has no integer author_person_id in history_context, but a matching connector-scoped PersonChannel (platform from context or provider) exists; request thread page/projection and assert root_message.display_name and person_id equal the mapped Person, with message_id equal the persisted parent-root UUID. Set explicit author_id and correct connector/platform; this proves fallback lookup rather than metadata integer lookup. Optionally use a second connector mapping of same author_id to a different Person to prove scope isolation.
4) Line 323: same root has neither valid author_person_id nor matching connector-scoped identity; give author_name "Unlinked sender" and author_id "unknown-author"; assert root_message.display_name == "Unlinked sender", person_id == nil, original author_id retained. An additional nil author_name/author_id case can assert "Person" if reachable with valid canonical message changeset; do not relax schema just for coverage.
5) Line 341: a real persisted Shared child transcript points to an existing parent but external_thread_id "missing-root-id" has no parent placement with that ID; attach a real non-assistant reply to the child. Project the scoped child and assert root_message == nil while title/participants/reply context remains sensible. This reaches author_person_id(nil) via stored_roots values; note that ordinary parent rows produce roots %{} and do NOT call this nil clause. If canonical capture refuses a rootless child, construct the intentionally incomplete historic child using Transcript.changeset/2 and TranscriptMessage.changeset/2 with parent permission coordinate, matching connector and unique scope_key. No production bypass.

Mocks/seams: none; DB/People/Engine remain real, no NodeRouter stub, network, app-env mutation, sleeps, timers, global Mox, or test-only production hooks. Keep async true with sandbox unless an actual shared-state dependency is discovered, then isolate only that scenario in async:false and restore shared state. Stable explicit timestamps only if order matters; no timing-based polling. Property assessment: these are five concrete persisted fallback branches, not broad input domains; no property test needed. If extending to connector-scope noninterference over many identities, consider bounded ExUnitProperties/StreamData, but a focused two-connector example is sufficient for this gap.

Reachability/blockers: line 341 requires a missing root in roots map (not merely a rootless top-level row). Verify schema/changeset and capture constraints before setup; if valid persisted child cannot be constructed, document the exact constraint and report line unreachable by public capture, do not weaken production or manufacture mocks. Verify whether line 301 title metadata survives capture; adapt DB arrangement through existing changesets only. Auth: project/1 trusts caller-scoped rows and must not be exposed as a public authorization API; no nil identity elevates access.

Action reuse assessment: not applicable—tests only, no executable operation or consumer change; reuse existing Engine projection, capture APIs and persisted schema builders as-is, no new Action/tool/workflow. Documentation: none (test-only). Validation handoff to parent: run isolated mix test test/zaq/engine/channel_history_projection_test.exs and targeted --cover for this file, inspect missed lines and branch assertions; parent owns mix q and coverage rerun, later final mix precommit only at approval gate. No full suite/coveralls in this task; record any unreachable line or changed coverage report explicitly. Planning agent must not execute tests or change Git files.
title: [zaq-ilh] [coverage] Cover ChannelHistoryProjection fallback and missing-root branches
